rows.title: Sella
rows.body:
Sella is one of the main crags in the Costa Blanca region. 

This extensive area offers many different types of climbing. Easy and mid grade sport routes are found at the most popular main crags in the centre of the valley, whilst mid to harder grade routes are concentrated in steeper sectors like the famous Wild Side. There are also mostly bolted multi-pitch climbs in Pared de Rosaria as well as entirely traditional routes in Puig Campana. All of this on great quality limestone!

Most of Sella’s  routes are up to 30 m of slabby or vertical,  fingery and technical climbing on little crimps and holes. 

The Costa Blanca's sunny weather makes it a brilliant climbing destination throughout the year. However, the best time to visit is from September until April. The most popular sectors in Sella have a Southerly orientation which makes them a perfect destination on sunny Winter days. Although the steep Sector Wild Side hardly ever gets the sun, summertime will generally be too hot unless you head for the North-facing crags like Pared de Rosaria.

Sella is also very convenient in terms of accommodation, transport and cost. It is only about a one hour drive from Alicante airport. The nearest big city is Benidorm which is only 40 minutes away by car. It is easy to reach the Sella and once there you feel far away from the crowded Benidorm beaches. The Costa Blanca has a wide choice of all types of accommodation according to your taste and budget, ranging from package deals in Benidorm hotels to apartments and villas in Sella, Finestrat and Villa Joyosa. As there is a lot of climbing outside the main valley it is definitely worth hiring a car to make the most of your holiday. Don't forget that in the Costa Blanca there is always an option of spending your rest days on the beach!

rows.title: Siurana
rows.body:
Everybody who climbs even a little will have heard of Siurana! It has been one of the most popular Spanish climbing destinations for many years, not only because it is home to La Rambla, one of the most famous 9a+’s in the world. 

Situated in the stunning Sierra de Prades mountains, it is less than an hour from other very important areas such as Margalef, Montsant, La Mussara  and Arboli. 

Siurana is a magical place with great scenery. The crags are situated inbetween the tiny picturesque hamlet of Siurana and its larger neighbour,  a village called Cornudella de Montsant. There are approximately 30 sectors and over 1200 routes, most of them of superb quality with new routes still being opened up all the time. 

Siurana is a great destination for mid to hard "7's" but grades range from 5s to 9's which makes it a good destination for groups of different climbing levels.  A typical Siurana route would be about 30 meters of technical fingery climbing on orange limestone with amazing views over the beautiful valley.

Thanks to its location, Cornudella has recently become a 'climbing village' as many Spanish, Catalan and foreign climbers  have started to settle down here. The bakery makes a convenient focal point and place to hang out whilst you decide on the day’s tick list. There is also a good climbing shop in the village. Cornudella has quite a good bus connection to the nearest big city, Reus. By car it takes only half an hour to get to Reus and about 2 hours to get to Barcelona. Both Barcelona and Reus have airports.

The best time to visit Sierra de Prades is from Spring to Autumn. In the Winter it might rain or snow and at these times the proximity of other areas  such as Margalef can offer a useful alternative. During late  Spring to early  Autumn it can get too hot for climbing on small ledges and crimps in the sun but you can always find some sectors in the shade to climb.

In Siurana there are various apartments for rent as well as rooms in the refuge in the town centre. If you prefer a lower-budget option, there is a campsite run by climbers very close to Siurana village. There are other campsites and refuges in Sierra de Prades at Uldemolins, Margalef, La Mussara as well.

To make the most of your trip a car is useful for getting to and from Cornudella although most crags are within walking distance from the Siuranna campsite.

rows.title: Cuenca
rows.body:
Cuenca belongs amongst the best sport climbing crags in Spain but for some reason it is not very well known abroad. It is situated in central Spain, only two hours from Madrid, which makes the area a favourite weekend destination for climbers from the capital. 

The sectors are located around Cuenca which is an UNESCO World Heritage Site. Cuenca is a medieval fortress town. It is quiet during the day but lively enough during the night. Its historical centre is definitely worth visiting even for those who are not particularly keen on sightseeing. 

The whole climbing area is pretty big and offers different types of crags full of excellent quality lines on solid yellow limestone. It is definitely famous above all for its rather short explosive routes though. Finger pockets, crimpers, slightly overhanging routes full of  bouldery moves, long reaches, athletic climbing...that's Cuenca and it is is definitely not easy. Climbing in the area actually started in the 80s as a result of a group of Madrid climbers' search for an area with a potential for hard routes.

We shouldn't forget though that there are more then 400 routes in Cuenca and especially some of the newer routes of middle grades are rather technical and fingery.  Nevertheless Cuenca is a place you go to enjoy middle to harder grades.

The best time to go to Cuenca is early Spring and late Autumn. Despite its location it gets very cold in the Winter (snow included) and far too warm in the Summer.

In the town itself you can choose from all types of accommodation and if you prefer there is a camp site situated 7 km from Cuenca. As in the case of most Spanish crags, it is recommendable to hire a car to be able to move around the sectors.

rows.title: Albarracin
rows.body:
Albarracin is definitely the most important Spanish bouldering area. No other area in Spain compares to it and it is often referred to as the Spanish Fontainebleau! Similarly,  the area is full of big reddish sandstone blocks scattered around a beautiful forest. The sandstone blocks are now full of boulder problems of all difficulties and styles: roofs with big jugs, overhangs with crimps as well as quality slabs. There are 15 different sectors,  some of which have climbing restrictions from January to August but this does not matter as when you come you will still always get a great choice of problems to solve!

The boulders are about a 5-minutes drive from Albarracin, a sleepy little tourist which is well worth visiting. Due to its medieval architecture Albarracin has been proposed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It offers nice walks along tiny medieval streets and quite a variety of little bars and restaurants where you can try the local specialities. It is a great option for your rest days, which are a necessity  in Albarracin. 

Getting there is easy as it is situated about 30 minutes from Teruel and 2 hours from Valencia, which has an International airport. If you can’t find flights to Valencia, you can check out Alicante as well. It would be best to hire a car so that you can move comfortably between the campsite (or town if you stay there) and the boulders. Hiring a car will also save a lot of time, which you can spend enjoying walks through the forest and getting to the boulders themselves. Some of the boulders are very close to the road whilst others are more remote and will take about half an hour to get to.

In Albarracin you can choose whatever type of accommodation best suits you, ranging from Bed&Breakfasts or campsites to more luxury options. The local campsite is a good choice if you come in Autumn or in Spring but in Winter the night temperatures get fall far below zero and there’s a possibility of snow. Albarracin’s ‘high season’ is from late Autumn to early Spring when the friction is great. but as mentioned above, count on with very cold nights and possible snow in Winter. As the boulders are all around the forest you can quite easily choose to climb in the sun or in the shade depending on the temperature, which is great.

rows.title: El Chorro
rows.body:
El Chorro is one of the oldest sport climbing areas in Andalusia. In fact, it belongs amongst one of the first areas to be bolted in Europe. The setting up of sport routes in El Chorro started in the 80s when the whole movement of sport climbing in Europe started to develop. Since then, sport climbing in El Chorro has spread to all of the surrounding cliffs and walls. As a result of this, El Chorro became one of the most popular climbing areas in Spain during the first decade of the 21st century. 

Nowadays, El Chorro has been overtaken in popularity by newer crags such as Oliana, Margalef and Rodellar in Northern Spain or Archidona, Otinar and Villanueva de Rosario in the South. Thanks to this decrease in popularity, El Chorro doesn't get as busy with climbers any more, which makes it actually even more worth visiting than before.

The little village of El Chorro is situated about 50 km inland from Malaga. It is set in beautiful landscape, in the gorge of El Chorro with the ridge of Las Frontales rising above it and surrounded by the beautiful Ardales lakes. 

All in all there are more than 1000 climbs which every climber can be satisfied with. El Chorro has a superb set of varied routes from long multi-pitch climbs to easily accessible sport lines with a great scale of grades. Those looking for the hardest grades will find them as well as those going a little easier or those operating in the easiest grades. El Chorro is very diverse when it comes to climbing styles as well:- tufas, steep walls, vertical crimpy climbing as well as good quality slabs, all on solid limestone rock.

The only problem you might encounter in El Chorro is that as the majority of the routes were bolted ages ago, some are very polished. This should not stop you from visiting the area though. For 7th grade and harder, make sure you check out magnificent Maquinodromo and its tufas as well as nearby Desplomilandia, which is a newer area full of beautiful lines where you won't complain about slippery footholds. 

Most of the crags are within walking distance of the village but having a car will make things easier, especially if you want to visit more remote crags such as Desplomilandia. Getting to El Chorro is much easier by car as well even though there is a train station in the village. Malaga is serviced by many low-cost airlines from all over Europe. 

For such a sleepy village, there are many accommodation options in El Chorro. There is a camp site literally next to one of the sectors, 3 climbing refuges and for those who want a little more luxury, there is the option of a hotel as well. 

One of the big pros of El Chorro is its mild climate. It has become popular as a Winter sport climbing venue. It is a great spot to enjoy climbing in the sun in wintertime and if it gets too warm you just change the sector and look for one that is in the shade. It might rain quite a lot though in Winter and as we all know, tufas filter and stay wet longer although in such circumstances, you can go for slaby and crimpy crags such as Las Frontales. In El Chorro you will always get to climb unless it is too hot so avoid the period from April till October.

You might have heard of Camino del Rey which would be an option for one of your rest days. This walkway goes along the whole length of the gorge and is suspended 100m above the ground. However, it is over 90 years old and is now falling apart although recently it has been made much safer due to the addition of via ferrate cables and bolts and is definitely worth visiting if you fancy a bit of a 'different' adventure.

rows.title: Rodellar
rows.body:
Rodellar is tufa-climbing paradise, a perfect destination for climbing holidays. Climbing huge overhanging walls is the most natural thing to do in this little village and everybody does it. 

Rodellar is more than just a climbing village though. It is a place with a special atmosphere. It is not just climbers who gather and live in Rodellar, it is a unique mixture of fanatic climbers and people who appreciate being in nature and living with slightly different values than most of today’s society. Rodellar is a little village with only about 30 locals but it is full of life. In summertime you can go climbing or canyoning but you can also attend joga classes, learn African dance and enjoy concerts and other cultural events such as flamenco shows or climbing presentations. 

It is located in the National park of Sierra de Guara, west of Barcelona about a 1 hour drive from a small Arragones town called Huesca. The whole area of Prepyrenees has great scenery. It is a hilly area full of rivers and gorges, which has made the area a world-class destination for canyoning as well. 

In Rodellar there are about 400 climbs bolted in two gorges: Mascún and Alcanadre. Even though it provides all the grades and vertical crags as well as big overhangs, what makes the area special are its tufas, huge caves and long and steep stamina routes. Alcanadre gorge is awesome but a little more remote and more difficult to access which makes it less visited. Nevertheless, climbing in Piscineta or Glacier is more than worth the hike!  Mascún gorge gets busier, especially in Rodellar's high season but it does not matter how busy it gets, it still is amazing. Climbing up 40m routes, which make it all the way up through the caves such as Gran Boveda and Surgencia is a feeling impossible to describe. 

Walking from the village, you get to all of the Mascún crags within 20 minutes which makes it possible to climb in two or three sectors in one day. Especially on hot, sunny days you will appreciate the possibility of having a refreshing swim in one of the beautiful ponds when going from one crag to another.  

As mentioned above, there are lines of all difficulties from 4th grade to 9A but Rodellar's best lines would be from 7Bs to 8Cs. Tufas, slopers, pinches, jugs, knee bars, dropped knees, heel hooks, dynos and a lot of endurance are Rodellar classics.

For many reasons it is considered to be a great spot to climb in Summer but in fact, the conditions are much better in late Spring and early Autumn. In Winter it is too cold and usually wet too as the tufas take their time to dry out after a couple of heavier rainfalls. The temperatures in summertime (especially in August) often don't drop below 30 degrees, which makes climbing the athletic long lines quite difficult. What makes Rodellar different from other areas in Arragon or Catalonia is the cold river very close to the crags and the fact that Rodellar is 'fanatic' even in Summer when everybody goes climbing even though it is too warm. Another disadvantage of summertime in Rodellar is that it gets too busy and not just with climbers so if you can choose, go at another time of year and risk a bit of rain. At the end of the day, if it rains in Rodellar you carry on climbing anyway! 

Rodellar is easy to get to. You can get a flight to Barcelona, Girona or Zaragoza and then hire a car (there is no bus that goes to Rodellar). You can then put up your tent in the campsite Mascún, rent a room in a climbing refuge in Kalandraka or rent an apartment in Hotel Valle de Rodellar and then forget about the car! There is another campsite down by the river called El Puente, which is used mainly by people who go canyoning as it is further away from the crags. There are three little food shops where you can get basic climbing gear as well but you will pay higher prices. If you feel like eating out, you can choose from many options.

rows.title: Frankenjura
rows.body:
Frankenjura is a perfect spot to spend your summer holidays, it does not matter whether you want to go really hard or just play around. There are almost 8000 climbs bolted in about 1000 smaller crags in this area and all of this in beautiful surroundings. The walls are hidden in pretty forests which provide a lot of necessary shade in the Summer and if it gets too warm, there are lots of little streams where you can always refresh yourself too. To make it an even more perfect place for every climber, Frankenjura offers all grades, from the easiest to the hardest.

It first became famous for different reasons though. It all started with legendary climbers such as Wolfgang Gulich and Kurt Albert setting up the hardest lines of the times and pushing the limits of what was possible. You will remember that Frankenjura is the home to world-famous sport climbing classics such as Sandstone and Action Direct!

Climbing in Frankenjura is hard and challenging. There are serious bouldery and explosive routes most of which don't reach more then 25 meters. There are a couple of lines reaching almost 40 meters but they are an exception though. The typical Frankenjura climb is full of one or two-finger pockets combined with holes and crimps and require a lot of finger strength and power endurance. If you prefer crimps and ledges there are sectors such as Student to choose from too.

The major crags are located around Pottenstein, Gosweinstein, Tuchersweld and Weischenfeld.  As the whole area is quite big, you will appreciate hiring a car which will make possible for you the typical Frankenjura fast sector shifts from hard to easier, from sunny to shady and from rainy to dry.

There are many good campsites in the area and most of the villages have Bed & Breakfasts and little supermarkets too. It is completely up to you what you go for. Your choice of accommodation will be influenced by the period in which you visit the place as well. In summertime campsites are good option but in Spring and Autumn you might choose better shelter in case it rains frequently.

Although Frankenjura has become a popular Summer climbing venue especially for climbers from Southern countries who run away from the heat, the ideal time to climb there is from early Spring to late Autumn, depending on each year's conditions as the weather there varies quite a lot. Some years it rains a lot, some years Summer gets too hot but in Frankenjura you will always find a spot to climb no matter how the weather is. If you like being cautious, check out the forecast for precipitation though!

rows.title: Gorges du Tarn
rows.body:
Georges de Tarn is one of the most important French sport climbing venues. It is set in a beautiful location and is home to more than 400 routes, most of which are of great quality. The whole area is full of beautiful fast flowing rivers, rocks and pine forests. Tarn isn't popular only for climbing- it is a favorite summer destination also for those who like kayaking, rafting and canyoning as well.  It is situated close to Millau (about 1 hour drive) in Southeast France - an area where you find good climbing of all styles everywhere you look. 

A great advantage of Gorges de Tarn as a climbing area is its wide range of lengths, styles and difficulties. It is a huge area with great potential for setting up new routes as only a small part of the gorge has been equipped so far. The rock there is limestone, often overhanging and full of pockets and crimps. Climbing there usually requires more stamina than power but there are sectors such as Gullich which offer short and power problems too. Climbing in Tarn is very varied and you will find climbs of all lengths there but the local specialty are the incredible pumpy stamina climbs such as those you find in a popular Tennessee sector. These are 50 to 70 m climbs mainly of the 7th grade which guarantee great fun. Another thing Tarn is famous for is its spaced bolting which adds a bit of special atmosphere to climbing there. It is safe but definitely needs more courage then what you are normally used to from other sport crags. There aren't many easier climbs than 6b or 6c but from 7a upward the place provides many top quality lines. 

A couple of years ago Tarn got 'famous' for its bad equipment with old bolts in a soft rock which unfortunately caused few bad accidents. As a result the whole area has been completely rebolted thanks to financial help from the local town hall. It is now equipped with good and solid bolts. 

The best time to visit is Spring and Autumn, Summers get too hot and Winters too cold. Nevertheless the crags get both sun and shade during the day which gives you a chance to get organized according to the weather. Even rain is not such a big problem in Tarn as there are some sectors which stay dry in the rain and the rest generally dries out faster than many other nearby areas. So Tarn is a good option during bad weather!

As it is a tourist venue there is a big choice of accommodation in the area. It has campsites (in the villages Le Rozier, Les Vignes etc.), small guest houses (in French usually called gites) and even free camping area.

rows.title: Val di Mello
rows.body:
This 'Little Yosemite' as it is often referred to, is an important and historical climbing area on the Italian-Swiss borders. It is where you will find some of the best granite climbing in Europe and it is also home to great bouldering and single pitch sport climbing. Val di Melo and Val Masino are set in beautiful Alpine scenery in a high valley close to a little picturesque village called San Martino. Just imagine the landscape! Everywhere you look you see mountains, rocks, blocks of boulders and greenery!

As mentioned above, the whole area offers all the types of climbing you can dream of: Bolted sport climbs and trad multi pitches as well as superb quality boulders. The rock is of great quality and as it is often weathered into fins and flutings which enables hard looking faces to be climbed also at moderate grades. Val di Melo is famous for its cracks and long slabs with hardly any holds (or what you usually call holds).  

Recently Val di Melo and Val Masino have become a top bouldering destination too. It is no surprise as the valley floor is covered with huge blocks which together with its colder climate makes it a perfect Summer venue for bouldering. Another pro of the Val di Melo boulders is that the landings are generally good and there are boulders of all heights. You just pick the one that inspires you and go for it!

When to go? Most of the sport and trad climbs are on South faces and are quite easy to approach. They are usually completely free from the snow by mid Summer. Remember that most of the mountain lines are at the altitude of between 2000 m and 3000m so the best time to visit is from July to early Autumn. For bouldering, you can come throughout the whole year, although the best time is October through to April in Val Masino and March through to November in Val di Melo. Rain can occur at any time in this mountainous area but at least the boulders dry quickly afterwards. 

Where to sleep? If you don't want to camp, you can choose from several alpine huts which serve the valley.

rows.title: Ceüse
rows.body:
Ceüse undoubtedly belongs among the best sport climbing crags in Europe. It is a great wall in a magical settings close to the Alps at an altitude over 1600 m. This makes it a perfect summer destination for all sport climbers who are willing to hike a little more than they usually do. The walk up takes a little more then one hour and just adds to all that makes Ceüse a very special place. After the hike you feel more worthy of the privilege of climbing in these great surroundings with these beautiful views. 

Climbing in Ceüse is very varied depending on the sector; from long pumpy climbs on big jugs such as those in La Cascade through long stamina routes (Berlin) to steep technical climbs in e.g  Demi Lune. Ceüse rock is awesome, luckily for all of us who love climbing, it is full of pockets. There are around 350 climbs which range from 5 to 9a+. However, the majority are the 7th grade  and the grading there is tough. Ceüse is not an ordinary sport climbing crag, similarly to Gorges de Tarn, it is well-known for its well-spaced bolts, which along with the settings add a special atmosphere to each climb, making it an unforgettable experience!

The best season is from late spring to early autumn. The variety of climbing allows you to choose the sun or the shade depending on the weather conditions. However, as with anywhere else in this area summers are very hot.

Most climbers stay at the convenient and economical Les Guerins campsite located right at the base of the hill. There is also an option of a free-camping area right below the hill close to the campsite and its little grocery shop. However, as it has no shade it can be quite uncomfortable on hot days. If you wish a bit more luxury there are many guesthouses in driving distance from the area.    

Ceüse is situated less than an hour drive from Gap in Sothern France, an area full of climbing crags. To get there you can fly to Grenoble, Marseille, Turin or Nimes. From all these airports it’s less then 2 hours drive to get to Ceüse.

rows.title: Zillertal
rows.body:
Zillertal climbing area is located in a beautiful alpine valley with tiny mountain rivers, lots of green, remote farms and high peaks around. There are granite blocks of all shapes and sizes scattered all around the valley and these offer loads of sport routes to choose from. Everything you ever dreamed of on granite: technical slabs, cracks, overhangs...Over last couple of years Zillertal has also become a popular destination for summer bouldering and if you feel like multipitch sport climbs Zillertal has a lot to offer too. There’s no mystery behind why the Innsbruck area has become a place where most of Austrian climbing freaks settle down! 

Zillertal is an Austrian granite paradise. There are 18 bouldering areas the biggest of which is at Zillerground  and offers 100 boulder problems. Most of the Zillertal boulders are in the forests so if you are looking for open space go to Berliner Hutte which has a more open feel. Do you prefer sport climbing to boulderig? There are around 15 sport crags with single pitches of 10 to 30m length and luckily some of them are cracks! As mentioned above apart from sport crags and boulders Zillertal has got its multipitch climbs too! Do you fancy multipitch climbing too? There are many alpine sport multipitches in Zillertal to choose from and some of them have up to 10 pitches! To sum it up there’s something for everyone in Zillertal, whether it’s granite, cracks, slabs, slopers or even steep crimpy overhangs!  

The crag is less than 1 hour drive from Innsbruck and very close to the High National Park, which starts at Ginzling. There are various airports you can fly to (Salzburg, Innsbruck or Munich) none of which are more then 1,5 hour drive  from Zillertal.

There are quite a few campsites in the area such as the one in Mayrohoten an as it’s  a key tourist area other types of accommodation (guesthouses etc.) can be easily arranged. Just find a place you like and enjoy the genuine Tyrolean hospitality.

The best season to come is from Spring to Autumn depending on what you want to focus on. To boulder you will wish for more friction and lower temperatures whereas to do some of the multipitches you will have to wait until they are free from snow.

rows.title: Český Ráj
rows.body:
Bohemian Paradise, the oldest nature reserve in the Czech Republic is a place you go to experience 'different climbing’ and there is no way you will regret it! It is worth visiting not just because of climbing but also to enjoy the unique natural beauties of the region; sandstone towers surrounded by pine forests, peaks and deep valleys that form a special scenery full of diversity, on only a few tens of square kilometres.

Bohemian Paradise lies only about an hour away from Prague but don’t worry because climbing here you will still feel far away from the capital. The towers form what the Czechs call ‘rock towns’. These are sandstone formations that have been sculpted over millions of years by the wind, rain, sun and frost. From the top of the towers you can see not only the magnificent rock towns but on a clear day, you can enjoy the view over the whole country.  

As the rock is very soft, you are not allowed to use chalk or top-rope (top-roping the rope leaves a mark on the soft rock) and for the same reason there are very little bolts (or none) compared to what we are used to from sport climbing in Europe. Partly this is to protect the area and partly it has to do with the special mentality of local climbers whose approach has always been very traditional and purist.

From the beginning, Czech sandstone climbing has been influenced by the Saxon approach and has accepted similar rules. As a result of this, a unique form of climbing has developed. Using friends, nuts etc is prohibited to protect the rock, as well as bolting the routes which means in Bohemian Paradise you have to place knots of different sizes for protection, which sounds odd but it works! Leave your chalk-bag at home because chalk is not allowed either as it leaves marks on the rock. It is all quite an adventure but it is such a unique experience that it makes it worthwhile. The towers are up to 25 m long and it is typical sandstone climbing - slabs, vertical and slightly overhanging faces with very tiny feet and small holds, cracks, crimps and slopers...in other words sandstone climbing is a great challenge for your technique and will test your balance.

Bohemian Paradise is an area where it is easy to enjoy your rest days as well. It has been recently proclaimed as an UNESCO Geo-Park, which is further proof of the charm of the whole place. If you feel like doing something a little bit different you can go on a hike to one of many observation towers or visit some of the little castles and chateaux the area is full of.

When to go? The weather in the Czech republic is not that easy to predict. The best period to enjoy the sandstone would be from early Spring to late Autumn. It can get too cold in the Spring and too warm in the Summer though and also watch out for the rain! Make sure you check out the weather forecast before you go... 

There are a few camp sites in the area or if you prefer a little more comfort, you can choose one of the B&Bs (in Czech usually called 'Pension’) in Hrubá Skála or Libošovice etc. Even though public transport within Czekia is not bad, you will appreciate hiring a car and having the option to explore the area more thoroughly.

rows.title: Arco
rows.body:
Arco has belonged amongst the most popular Italian crags for decades. It lies in Northern Italy (Trentino), close to the beautiful Lake Garda, which is a well-known location to all sailing and MTB fanatics as well. The small town of Arco is very picturesque and apart from climbing has a lot of other things to offer, not only great food and wine, pretty architecture, well stocked climbing and MTB shops but also very friendly people and chilled atmosphere. Arco climbing area is very convenient in terms of having a wide range of grades, climbing styles and easy accessibility to the majority of the crags. It really has something for everybody, multi-pitch routes on big walls as well as a great variety of sport crags of different lengths, difficulties and styles. 

The rock at Arco is superb limestone. It is preferable though to have a guide with you to show you the best places to climb where the rock is not too polished. And you bet there are sectors to choose from! There are thousands of sport climbs in over 50 sectors in the area. The Arco rock seems to be just perfect to climb. It is covered with pockets and tufas and forms amazing overhangs. It offers great climbs in beautiful scenery and there is a friendly atmosphere in the sectors!

If you fancy big walls, in Arco there are about 30 multi-pitch sectors you can choose from. They are Dolomite-style big wall routes on steep limestone and some of them reach up to 1400m. The majority of the multi-pitch climbs are of 200-600m and naturally they require you to use protection such as cams and friends. 

The best seasons for climbing in Arco are Spring and Autumn but Summer temperatures are more appropriate for sunbathing at Lake Garda than for climbing.  

The whole area is very touristic which allows you to choose from all different types of accommodation: campsites, apartments, guesthouses and hotels...

rows.title: Ardeche
rows.body:
The Ardeche is known as the adventurer's paradise.  It is located close to Lyon in Southeastern France. It would be hard to find a better place for family climbing holidays. Ardeche gorge has got it all; beautiful settings, great weather, plenty of climbs in lower grades, there is always a river nearby to refresh yourself in and on top of that there is an option of combining climbing with many other adventure activities such as canyoning or canoeing. 

The Ardeche is a great crag for beginners and children. It is a huge area with a majority of easy single-pitch climbs. However, you will also find sport climbs of the eighth grade there and multi-pitch routes of all difficulties too. There are literally thousands of sport climbs; all of which are well bolted but unfortunately some crags are very polished. The main Ardeche sectors are limestone but further North you will find granite crags as well as easy bouldering areas.  The Ardeche provides you with all you need really but you do not go to the Ardeche to crank it hard though.

The best time to visit for the best climbing conditions is early Spring through to Autumn. Summers are too hot for serious climbing but you can still combine climbing in the shade with water sports and other activities that the area offers. The whole area is very popular among sporty tourists from all over Europe which unfortunately makes it very crowded during school and public holidays so if you can, try to avoid these periods.

As the area is very popular with tourists, there are a great variety of accommodation types you can choose from: campsites, guest houses and hotels. In the high season you might need to make reservations well in advance though.

The closest airports are in Avignon, Nimes and Lyon which are all less than 2 hours drive away. There is a good railway network in France but you will need to rent a car to get around.

rows.title: Terradets
rows.body:
"The southern runoffs of the Pyrenees offer an enormous potential for sports climbing - a drive from Barcellona westwards convinces impressively. Balaguer, just north of Lleida, is home to important crags such as St. Llorenc de Montgai and Camarasa and also Terradets which, with its recently developed sector Les Bruixes, offers some of the best soprts climbing in Spain. The sector slants leftwards and is characterised by steeply overhanging stamina climbing up tufas, pockets and... tufas once again. Resistencia pura!"Nowadays Terradets is well-known mainly for the fantastic and hard sport climbing in Paret de les Bruixes but it has much more to offer because in Terradets you will find great climbs of easier grades and superb quality multi-pitch routes too. It is located North of Lleida which is an area considered a Catalan sport climbing paradise and is a place which has recently become a top destination for world's best climbers. The area is literally packed with great crags such as Oliana, Santa Linea, Tres Ponts, Collegats, Camarasa and many more...Nevertheless Pared de les Bruixes is definitely one of the best sport crags of hard 7th and lower 8th grade in Spain. 

The rock in Terradets is superb limestone but compared to the other crags in the North of Lleida, bolting there had started earlier. Especially in the high-grade sport crag Paret de les Bruixes, you must be prepared for polished rock. The footholds might be black and shiny but still the climbs there are superb and a must-visit! It is impossible not to enjoy the steep tufa routes with a lot of sidepoles, slopers as well as little crimpers. There are long stamina routes but also long lines with bouldery problems. If you get bored of tufas (which is not likely to happen), you can move on to the left part of the crag where you find few rather vertical and crimpy climbs of superb quality too. 

If you want to go a little easier, visit Les Bruixes Norte which offers same quality routes but  in slightly easier grades or try sector Si fas free no fa fret (part of multi-pitch crag Paret de les Bagasses) and its 5th and 6th single or two pitch routes. Remember though that both the sectors are in the shade for most of the day. As mentioned above, there are also two superb multi-pitch walls called Roca Regina and  Paret de les Bagasses. 

Climbing days in Terradets are always short, no matter when you come. The best conditions are in late Autumn and Winter. Especially in Les Bruixes on the polished rock you really do appreciate good friction. It is South facing so the best are cold sunny winter days but you can easily climb on warmer cloudy autumn days too. Because of the nearby dam, the crag often remains foggy and humid until around a noon or later which makes the climbing days even shorter. The best time to go to Bruixes Norte and  Paret de les Bagasses is Autumn and Spring.

There is a nice and friendly climbing refuge in the nearby village of Cellers which is also very warm and therefore will be appreciated especially in the winter. Another option is a hotel in Cellers. If you don't mind driving about half an hour, there are a lot of nice places to rent in the nearby villages too. 

Fly to Barcelona which is about 3 hours drive from Terradets. If you want to avoid renting a car you can stay in the refuge in Cellers which is walking distance from Paret de les Bruixes but if you want to visit more sectors you will appreciate renting a car.

rows.title: Oliana
rows.body:
Nowadays Oliana is one of the most famous Spanish crags. It is well known abroad especially because of ‘La dura dura’, Chris Sharma’s great project of 9B+. It has a high concentration of hard-grade routes, most of which are great quality and as a result Oliana has recently become a popular destination for the strongest climbers in the world. 

Oliana is situated about 90 km north of Lleida (a Catalan town lying about 150km east of Barcelona). The whole area to the north of Lleida is now considered to be one the best sport climbing areas in the world as it is home to many top quality crags.  There are crags of all types (from all difficulty sport climbing areas to sandstone bouldering and the multi-pitch classics). 

Oliana is a high overhanging limestone wall with no more than 30 routes from 7a to 9b+, most of which are up to 50 meters long. Sustained athletic climbing on tufas, big pockets as well as crimps and a lot of stamina is what you will find in Oliana and it is fantastic! Just count on the fact that to really appreciate the wall you will want to be able to climb 8a's or 8apluses.

Apart from the main sector of Contrafort de Rumbau, there are low to middle-grade climb options in La Paret de l’ Obaga Negra which offers slab and vertical routes worth trying as well. 

The best time to go to Oliana is wintertime. The crag is in the sun from the morning until about 4pm or 5pm, depending on the line. You must count on shorter climbing days though as it often takes a long time before the morning fog disappears and as soon as the wall gets in the shade it gets too cold. On colder Autumn and Spring days you might get good climbing conditions too but remember that the noonday sun gets very strong. 

Even though the wall is situated close to the village of Oliana you will need a car. There are little hotels and guesthouses in Oliana as well as in the nearby villages which you might find convenient, especially in Winter as it gets very cold in the area.

rows.title: Montgrony
rows.body:
Montgrony is one of the old Spanish crags situated in the central Pyrenees close to a little village called Gombren. Although Montgrony is not that famous abroad it is worth visiting! Climbing there is not as ‘rewarding’ as in some other areas such as Rodellar or Terradets. Similarly it is tufa climbing but the routes are mostly shorter, more bouldery and explosive, in other words a little less ‘comfortable’ to climb. But don’t hesitate to come! It is great tufa climbing on a superb rock away from the crowds and in beautiful scenery. 

Montgrony is not a big area, all in all there are about 300 routes, most of which are the 7th and the 8th grade. As mentioned above it is mainly tufa climbing on big jugs but bouldery and very physical so get your power endurance ready!

The best time to come is from Autumn to Spring as most of the walls are south facing. Despite its altitude, Montgrony gets quite hot the sun even on winter days but when the sun goes down you will need your down jackets!

Mongrony is one hour from Girona, close to Gombren, so the ideal way to get there is to take a plane to Girona, which is operated mainly by low-cost airlines, and then to hire a car. There is a little refuge close to the crags but it is still a drive away. Climbing in Montgrony you will definitely need a car or better still, a camper, which would be the best option as there is a pretty car park literally next to the crags.

rows.title: Margalef
rows.body:
There is no need to say much about Margalef as it is very well known abroad as well as in Spain. There is no doubt that it is one of the most favourite Spanish crags. It is situated in the beautiful scenery of the Montsant Natural Park, 1 hour away from Lleida and about 2 hours away from Barcelona.

Margalef is a little sleepy village of thirty houses, one local bar, a climbing refuge, a cheap hotel and a restaurant. 

The crags are scattered around two little canyons, all very close to each other. Margalef rock is a conglomerate, not too solid but great anyway. Climbing there is peculiar as you mostly climb over one, two or three finger pockets together with some slopers and crimps and at some sectors, tufas as well. You can find great lines of all difficulties from the 5th grade to the 9th, which is one of the reasons why the area is so popular. Another reason is that once you get used to the style, redpointing there is not as difficult as in more demanding areas such as nearby Siurana. The grades in Margalef are little softer as well but it doesn't take any qualities away from the place. It is superb, good fun climbing in great scenery where everybody finds what they look for; more remote, quiet and tranquil crags such as Catedral and Ermita or always busy and fanatic crags literally just off the road such as Raco de Finestra or Laboratori. Margalef offers its typical slightly overhanging or vertical technical lines as well as slabs, steep overhangs and even some tufas too!

The whole area has developed very quickly and thanks to some local climbers there are a couple of new routes bolted every month and still there are loads of rocks left to be equipped in the future.

The weather in Margalef is very convenient as well, the best time to come is from late Autumn to Spring. Every day when you wake up you simply check out the weather and decide whether to go to the shade or to the sun as there are crags in all orientations. Probably the best time to come though is in the Winter when you can climb in Espadelles, Ermita, Cabernet in the sun and enjoy the great friction.

The only problem in Margalef is that as we said before it gets very busy especially during Bank Holidays and weekends so remember to check out Spanish and French Bank Holidays before you book your vacation if you don't like climbing in the crowds.

Getting to Margalef is easy. You can fly to Barcelona or Girona and hire a car as you will need one to get to the crags in Margalef itself. If you stay longer don't forget to check out nearby crags like Siurana, Arboli or Montsant which are all worth visiting as well. The whole province of Catalonia is now considered to be the place with the highest number of great quality sport climbing areas in the world.

There is no camp site in Margalef yet but close to the dam there is a free camping area and apart from that you have many options of economical accommodation from a refuge to apartments for rent or a cheap hotel down in the village. When staying in Margalef please help to protect the nature and do not leave any rubbish anywhere. It is one of the places where the locals have always been very friendly and welcoming to the climbers since they started to come but sadly over last couple of years it has been made clear that not even climbers know how to behave in nature.

rows.title: Finale Ligure
rows.body:
Finale is situated on the Mediterranean coast near Savona and certainly belongs amongst Italy’s most popular sport climbing crags. It is a huge area of over 10 square km of crags and nearly 3000 routes, which offers climbing of great quality and variety too. The rock there is marine white limestone and the landscape is beautiful although slightly uncommon for sport crags as it is very harsh and green. A small disadvantage of the area is that it is very popular with tourists and therefore at times it is very crowded and also some areas are too close to motorways.

In Finale you will find a great variety of climbing styles to choose from; smooth slabs, vertical walls as well as steep overhangs. You have a great choice of grades there too, from 4's to 8's but the majority of the lines will be within the 6th and lower 7th grade. No matter what grade you climb though, get ready for some good technical climbing! There are mainly single-pitch routes but if you suddenly feel like longer routes you can always visit Bric pianarella – Finale's 'big wall' with routes up to 250m long. 

Finale provides crags of all directions which makes it possible to climb there throughout the year but you get the best climbing conditions in most of the crags is Spring and Autumn. In Winter the main problem is that the weather can be quite unpredictable. 

As mentioned above, Finale is located on the Mediterranean coast and naturally is a popular tourist destination, which is an advantage when it comes to accommodation. You can really choose from all kinds of facilities according to your taste. 

It is very easy to get there as it takes only 30 minutes to drive from Genova international airport but as it is a big area you will appreciate renting a car to get around.

rows.title: Mallorca
rows.body:
In Spain, Mallorca is known as the best Deep-Water Soloing area, although recently it has become a popular destination for sport climbing and those who go there come back impressed by the quality and quantity of the rock. Mallorca has something for everybody: tufas, roofs with big jugs, overhangs as well as cracks and slabs, all difficulties included and all on great solid rock. Sport climbing in Mallorca will definitely carry on growing, as there is a great amount of rock to be bolted.  

The western side of Mallorca is where you find most of sport climbing crags, all of them easily approachable from Palma or Soller. Mallorca is a small island and has a good road network, which makes it possible to visit many crags from one base.

You will want to go to the east if you prefer DWS.  Most of the cliffs are situated close to Porto and Santanyj. On this side of Mallorca there are only few sport climbing areas but they are worth visiting as well.

The best time to go is any time of the year really apart from the Summer. This is when Mallorca becomes packed with people and far too hot. If you avoid summertime, you will visit a lovely quiet island with mild weather. The only problem is the humidity so you will have to get used to a little worse friction on humid days.  

How to get there? Fly to Palma de Mallorca using one of many low-cost airlines, hire a car, choose a good base in the area you want to climb in and then enjoy this magnificent island!

rows.title: Kalymnos
rows.body:
Kalymnos is now well known to everybody who climbs a little because this pretty little Greek Island has an incredible amount of rock to offer. There is a high concentration of superb routes on only a few square kilometers and new ones are constantly being added. It is a great destination for both fanatic climbing trips and chilled family climbing holidays. There are not many places in Europe where in the morning you can climb in amazing caves full of tufas, in the afternoon sunbathe on beautiful beaches and in the evening have a drink and chat with other climbers in one of many cozy bars on the island. 

There are around 64 sectors bolted on the island, all of them on solid limestone. On some crags the rock is a little sharp and on others it is a little polished but there are so many climbs to choose from that it does not really bother anybody. With such a quantity of rock in Kalymnos you find all types of climbing styles from delicate slabs and vertical crimpy walls, pumpy climbs on big jugs to spectacular tufa climbing. Kalymnos tufa climbing is different from anywhere else for two reasons. First, on crags such as Grand Grota, the tufas are huge and everywhere you look. You have to literally find your way up through them holding onto them, stepping on them and squeezing in between them. Don't forget to get your knee bars and heel hooks right otherwise you won't get too far! Secondly, in Kalymnos you get to climb superb quality tufa lines not only in hard grades but also in the 6th and easy 7th grade. Most of the climbs are single pitches but there are also many 2 or 3 pitch stamina routes in sectors such as Panorama or Sikati cave. You might need to get used to a little strange friction though, as on all seaside crags there is usually more humidity in the air. 

There are a couple of villages on the island where climbers usually stay. The majority usually stay in Masouri or Armeos both of which are close to the most popular crags and offer accommodation ranging from hotels, budget hotels, Bed&Breakfasts to apartments for rent. There is no free camping allowed on the island though.

You can either fly to the nearby island of Kos which is serviced by low cost airlines and then take a ferry to Mastichari port or you can fly straight to Kalymnos airport which has a connection from Athens but the flights sometimes get canceled due to high winds.

The best time to visit is April through to May and then from October to November when the island is not as busy with tourists and also is a little cooler. The climate in Kalymnos is quite dry which makes it possible to climb throughout the whole year. Most of the crags are in the shade in the morning so if you get your timings right, you can always get decent climbing conditions. In the Summer it gets too hot for serious climbing though. In Winter you can climb in the afternoon as most of the crags are South facing but mind the rain because once the tufas get wet they take their time to dry out.

rows.title: Etxauri
rows.body:
Etxauri lies in a climbing paradise of Basque country. Basque country is a unique place with an unusually high concentration of great quality crags and also climbing fanatics. The whole area has a long climbing tradition and Etxauri in particular belongs among the classics of the area. It is set in a beautiful scenery, offers great quality solid limestone and on top of that, is very easy to get to – it lies only 15 km away from Pamplona!

Etxauri is a one of those places which you simply can't miss out if you like challenging technical climbing. There are more than 800 lines of all grades and climbing styles. As mentioned above, its specialty is challenging technical climbing. Little crimps and hardly any footholds on slabby, vertical or slightly overhanging faces – that is Etxauri's classics and that obviously requires great amount of technique and skill. 

Etxauri is a huge area and offers great variety of climbing. Apart from the main sport crags, there are good quality multipitches areas and also interesting little sport areas such as San Fausto, which are definitely worth your attention too. 

Most of the popular crags are on the sun which makes Etxauri great spot to enjoy sun when the temperatures drop down. You can come in autumn or spring but make sure you avoid summertime. If you wish to come in winter, you can try but count on with very low temperatures on cloudy days and a high probability of rain.

To get to Basque country you can fly into Bilbao, Vitoria or San Sebastian, all of which are less than 2 hours away from Pamplona. The closest is San Sebastian which is about only about an hour drive from Pamplona. Like everywhere in Spain you will get around much better in a rented car than in public transport.

When it comes to where to sleep, in the Etxauri area you have a great choice: There are 3 campsites nearby Pamplona or you can simply visit Pamplona and choose what you like. Those of you who are used to Mediterranean mild temperatures  shouldn't forget that the climate in Basque country is rather different from Spain. It is much colder at night and rainier especially during spring, autumn and winter. Another thing which makes the area different from the rest of the country are the prices – Basque country is one of the most expensive provinces in Spain.

rows.title: Gorges du Verdon
rows.body:
Verdon is one of the best European crag which offers a wide range of climbing styles in a really unique place. Climbing there is a special experience not only for the superb quality limestone but also for the breathtaking scenery. The crags spread on both sides of the river Verdon as it carves its way through the 100's metres high gorge.

There are more than 1000 routes of all grades and styles, from short friendly sport climbs to impressive big wall routes both bolted and traditional protection. The gorge is huge and therefore usually divided in 3 parts: Upstream Gorge, Central Gorge and Downstream Gorge. Majority of the climbs are challenging vertical walls with perfect holds and cracks but you may find top quality tufa climbs too.

Verdon offers endless rock of an incredible quality and stunning views but it is not for free.

Climbing there requires a lot of commitment. Its specialty is that to most of the routes you have to abseil down, pull the ropes and climb out. Those of you who like exposure will fall in love with Verdon immediately. Verdon is a quiet crag where you can experience real authentic moments climbing with no one around.

The majority of the climbs are easily accessed from car parks along the road (max 20 minutes walk). Some of the routes start at the bottom of the canyon and for those, you have to hike through a system of tunnels which is an adventure in itself. The best season to go is from late spring through autumn, though watch out for afternoon thunderstorms, which are not uncommon in August and September. In the winter it gets cold and wet.

There is a good campsite in the nearby village called La Palud-sur- Verdon.

The crag is located about 2 hours from Cannes or Marseille and easy to reach by car.

rows.title: Chamonix
rows.body:
This mountain village is definitely one of the best places in the world for many outdoor activities such as mountaineering, trad climbing and skiing. It is often referred to as the Capital of world climbing and it really has a lot to offer. Chamonix means superb granite rock and gneiss set in stunning scenery of high mountains. The village is dominated by Mont Blanc, the highest mountain of the Alps, which rises 4808m above sea level so naturally, climbing in Chamonix guarantees an authentic Alpine experience. To access many of the classic routes, you have to cross a glacier and the routes themselves require more commitment than ordinary trad climbs so the trip is rather suitable for clients with some previous experience.

Chamonix is not famous only for granite cracks and fine slabs of the Mont Blanc massif, but also for the lower and sunnier gneiss of Aguillle Rouges.

Obviously in the Alps, one has to be careful about the weather but on the other hand, the crags in Chamonix are at very different altitudes which gives you the option to choose the most suitable crag depending on the time of the year. Nevertheless, the best season is summertime when the days are long and when even the higher crags are snow free. Lower down in the nearby valleys, there are some areas with easy access where you can climb later into the autumn.

Chamonix is a great destination not only for trad climbers and high mountain lovers but also for those who prefer sport climbing or bouldering. From Le Fayet all the way to Switzerland, there are several valleys which are snow free from late spring and offer good quality sport climbing. Climbing on these crags, you can choose from a wide range of grades and lines. The rock here is somewhat peculiar because it is a mixture between granite and granter greiss . Yo can go for single pitch sport routes as well as well as equipped multipitches.

If you feel like bouldering, in Chamonix is also the right place for you. There are great boulder problems scattered around the area, some of them isolated and some of them gathered in circuits like in Fontainebleau. The rock is of great variety: from high mountain limestone in places such as Le Col de la Colombiere to granite in e.g. Les Bossons and superb quality greiss boulders in Medonnet area.

The boulder areas are located at different altitudes so you can come almost whenever you like and choose the most suitable boulder zone according to the weather.

rows.title: George de la Jonte
rows.body:
We decided to add to the list of Rockbusters' destinations another top quality French crag, Gorge de la Jonte with more than 300 superb routes reaching about 150m in height. Surprisingly, La Jonte isn't well known by foreign climbers although it is just around the corner from the popular climbing site called Gorges du Tarn (the region of Millau).

Gorge de la Jonte has a long climbing history. Many of its climbs were open before the era of bolting and nowadays there still remains many routes traditionally-protected. It is a great site for climbers who like exposure and more adventurous climbing. Count on with an old style french grading, though. Many grades will probably feel tough in comparison to nearby Tarn or other European crags so especially when choosing your first multipitch routes be careful. La Jonte offers quite a variety of single and multipitch routes, both bolted and traditional. The rock is solid limestone with pockets, slopers and holes and the terrain is mostly vertical or steep. To sum it up, the gorge has loads of great climbs in a magnificent setting and is definitely worth visiting.

Majority of the climbs face south and get a lot of sun, therefore the best season is from autumn through late spring. However, the routes following corners get sun or shade depending on the time of the day and higher up on long climbs you usually get cold breeze which makes it possible to climb them even on hot days.

rows.title: Les Calanques de Marseille
rows.body:
This rock climbing area is located in southern France and stretches from Marseille to the little town of Cassis. It is large and is usually divided in 8 main areas, each of which is very different. Climbing there varies enormously from single pitch sport climbs, long multipitch climbs reaching 250m in height, to deep water soloing (DWS).

Similarly, the limestone rock is different on each crag and offers a great variety of climbing styles, from technical slabs to climbing on steep seaside cliffs and in overhanging caves. In terms of difficulty, again, what you find in Les Calanques is a wide range of grades.

There are about 2500 bolted routes and about 1000 trad climbs. In fact, Calanque belongs among France's largest rock climbing areas.

Climbing in Calanque is possible throughout the year, the best conditions are during the spring, though. South-facing crags are a good alternative for climbing in the winter because these crags are usually also sheltered from the Mistral wind. On summer days you can go DWS or head to some of the north-facing cliffs. In the autumn you are likely to get a lot of rainy days.

Conquer New Heights: A Guide to Rock Climbing in Istria, Croatia


When it comes to rock climbing, Istria, Croatia is a hidden gem that should not be overlooked. With its breathtaking landscapes, diverse climbing routes, and vibrant climbing community, Istria offers an unforgettable experience for both beginners and seasoned climbers alike.

One of the main reasons to choose Istria for rock climbing is the sheer variety of climbing options available. From limestone cliffs to deep water soloing, Istria has it all. The region is known for its sport climbing, which involves climbing routes that are pre-equipped with fixed bolts for protection. This makes it an ideal destination for climbers of all levels, as there are routes suited for beginners as well as more challenging ones for advanced climbers.

In addition to the diverse climbing options, Istria's stunning natural beauty adds to the allure of the region. Imagine climbing up a limestone cliff, surrounded by crystal-clear waters and lush greenery. The picturesque landscapes of Istria make every climb a memorable experience. Whether you are climbing in the early morning light or enjoying a sunset climb, the beauty of Istria will leave you in awe.

 

Rock climbing in Istria: A brief overview

Rock climbing has a rich history in Istria, dating back several decades. The region has attracted climbers from all over the world, who come to experience the unique challenges and rewards that Istria has to offer. Istria is located in the heart of Europe, making it easily accessible for climbers from all corners of the globe.

One of the defining characteristics of rock climbing in Istria is the abundance of limestone cliffs. These cliffs provide a solid and reliable surface for climbing, making it a favorite among climbers. The routes vary in difficulty, ranging from easy routes suitable for beginners to more challenging routes that will test even the most experienced climbers.

Apart from limestone cliffs, Istria also offers opportunities for deep-water soloing. This thrilling form of climbing involves climbing without the use of ropes or other protective equipment, relying solely on your skills and the water below you. Istria's crystal-clear waters make it an ideal destination for deep-water soloing, providing a unique and exhilarating experience for climbers.

 

The best rock climbing spots in Istria, Croatia

Istria is home to numerous rock climbing spots that cater to climbers of all levels. Here are some of the best spots that should be on your climbing itinerary in Istria:

1. Rovinj

Rovinj is a charming coastal town that offers a great climbing experience. The cliffs here provide a mix of easy and moderate routes, making it perfect for beginners and those looking to improve their skills. The routes in Rovinj offer stunning views of the Adriatic Sea, adding to the overall experience.

2. Limski Kanal

Limski Kanal, also known as Lim Fjord, is a popular climbing spot in Istria. The limestone cliffs here offer a range of routes, from easy to challenging. The fjord itself adds a unique touch to the climbing experience, with its tranquil waters and stunning scenery.

3. Vela Draga

Vela Draga is a hidden gem for climbers in Istria. Tucked away in the Učka Nature Park, this climbing spot offers a peaceful and secluded environment for climbers. The routes here are varied, with options for both sport climbing and deep water soloing. The breathtaking views from the top make the climb well worth it.

These are just a few of the many rock climbing spots in Istria. Each spot has its own unique charm and challenges, ensuring that climbers of all levels will find something to suit their preferences.

 

Essential gear and equipment for rock climbing in Istria

Before embarking on your rock climbing adventure in Istria, it is essential to have the right gear and equipment. Here is a list of the essentials you'll need to ensure a safe and enjoyable climb:

  •     Climbing shoes: A good pair of climbing shoes is crucial for maintaining grip and stability on the rock. Choose a pair that fits snugly and provides enough support for your feet.
  •     Harness: A harness is a vital piece of equipment that connects you to the rope and provides support during your climb. Make sure your harness fits properly and is comfortable to wear for long periods.
  •     Helmet: Safety should always be a priority when rock climbing. A helmet will protect your head from falling rocks or accidental impacts.
  •     Chalk bag: Chalk helps to keep your hands dry and improve your grip while climbing. A chalk bag attached to your harness allows for easy access during your climb.
  •     Belay device: A belay device is used to control the rope while belaying your partner. Choose a device that is appropriate for your climbing style and level of experience.
  •     Quickdraws: Quickdraws are used to connect your rope to the bolts on the climbing route. It is essential to have enough quickdraws to safely climb the route.
  •     Rope: A dynamic rope is used for lead climbing and top-roping. Ensure that your rope is in good condition and appropriate for the routes you plan to climb.
  •     Carabiners: Carabiners are used to connect various pieces of climbing equipment together. Make sure you have enough carabiners for your gear and additional equipment.

Having the right gear not only ensures your safety but also enhances your overall climbing experience. Invest in quality equipment and regularly check for any signs of wear or damage.

Take a leisurely stroll through the narrow streets, visit historical sites, and indulge in the local cuisine.

Are you ready to take your rock climbing skills to new heights? Look no further than the captivating island of Hvar, a hidden gem in the Adriatic Sea. With its rugged cliffs, pristine beaches, and warm Mediterranean weather, Hvar offers a truly unparalleled rock climbing experience for both beginners and seasoned climbers alike. Whether you're a thrill-seeker or simply seeking a new adventure, Hvar has something for everyone. Challenge yourself on the limestone cliffs of Sveta Nedilja, where you'll find routes that cater to all skill levels. As you ascend, you'll be rewarded with breathtaking views of the turquoise waters below.


The Best Rock Climbing Spots in Hvar

When it comes to rock climbing, Hvar boasts some of the most impressive climbing spots in Europe. One of the top destinations for rock climbers is Sveta Nedilja, located on the southern coast of the island. This picturesque village is nestled at the foot of towering limestone cliffs, offering a wide range of routes suitable for climbers of all abilities. From gentle slab climbs to challenging overhangs, Sveta Nedilja has it all. The unique geological formations in this area provide a diverse range of climbing experiences, ensuring that every climb is a memorable one.

Another popular spot for rock climbing in Hvar is Dubovica Beach. This stunning beach is not only a great place to relax and soak up the sun but also offers a unique climbing experience. Ancient ruins provide a dramatic backdrop for your climb, adding a touch of history and culture to your adventure. The cliffs at Dubovica Beach offer a variety of routes, from easy climbs for beginners to more challenging routes for experienced climbers. No matter your skill level, you'll find something to suit your abilities and make your climb unforgettable.


Safety Measures and Equipment for Rock Climbing

Safety should always be the top priority when engaging in any outdoor activity, and rock climbing is no exception. Before embarking on your rock climbing adventure in Hvar, it's important to ensure that you have the necessary safety measures in place. This includes using proper climbing equipment such as helmets, harnesses, and ropes. It's also essential to have a basic understanding of climbing techniques and safety protocols. If you're new to rock climbing, consider taking a beginner's course or hiring a certified guide who can teach you the fundamentals and ensure your safety throughout your climb.


Tips for Beginners in Rock Climbing

If you're new to rock climbing, Hvar is the perfect place to start your climbing journey. With its diverse range of climbing routes and experienced guides, you'll have everything you need to learn the ropes and build your skills. Here are a few tips to help beginners get started:

    Start with easy climbs: Begin with routes that are suitable for beginners. These routes typically have larger holds and less challenging movements, allowing you to focus on building your technique and confidence.
    Take breaks and hydrate: Rock climbing can be physically demanding, so it's important to take breaks and stay hydrated. Bring plenty of water and listen to your body to avoid overexertion.
    Practice proper footwork: Footwork is crucial in rock climbing. Focus on placing your feet accurately and using your legs to generate power, rather than relying solely on your upper body strength.
    Learn to fall safely: Falling is a part of rock climbing, but learning to fall safely can help prevent injuries. Practice falling onto crash pads or in controlled environments to build confidence and reduce the risk of injury.
    Enjoy the journey: Remember to have fun and enjoy the process. Rock climbing is not just about reaching the top but also about the experience and the personal growth that comes with it.


Advanced Techniques and Challenges in Rock Climbing

For experienced climbers looking for a challenge, Hvar offers a range of advanced climbing routes and techniques to test your skills. The limestone cliffs of Sveta Nedilja provide a playground for climbers seeking more difficult climbs. From steep overhangs to technical face climbs, there are plenty of routes that will push your limits and provide an adrenaline rush like no other. Advanced techniques such as dynos, heel hooks, and crimping will come into play as you navigate the challenging terrain. However, always remember to prioritize safety and only attempt routes that are within your skill level.


Best Time to Go Rock Climbing in Hvar

While Hvar's Mediterranean climate means that rock climbing is possible year-round, the best time to go depends on personal preferences and weather conditions. The peak climbing season in Hvar is during the spring and fall when temperatures are mild, and the weather is generally stable. During these seasons, you can enjoy cooler temperatures, fewer crowds, and optimal climbing conditions. However, if you prefer warmer weather and longer days, summer can also be a great time to climb in Hvar. Just be prepared for higher temperatures and more tourists. It's always a good idea to check the weather forecast and plan your climb accordingly to ensure the best possible experience.


Rock Climbing Competitions and Events in Hvar

Hvar has gained recognition as a premier rock climbing destination, attracting climbers from around the world. As a result, the island hosts various rock climbing competitions and events throughout the year. These events not only showcase the skills of professional climbers but also provide opportunities for enthusiasts to witness the sport in action and participate in friendly competitions. Whether you're a spectator or a competitor, these events offer a unique chance to immerse yourself in the vibrant rock-climbing community of Hvar and connect with like-minded individuals who share your passion for the sport.


Rock Climbing Community in Hvar

Hvar is not only known for its breathtaking climbing spots but also its welcoming and vibrant rock climbing community. Whether you're a local or a visitor, you'll find a supportive and inclusive community of climbers who are passionate about the sport. From climbing clubs and meetups to social media groups, there are various ways to connect with fellow climbers and share experiences, tips, and advice. The community is open to climbers of all levels, and you'll often find climbers willing to lend a helping hand or offer guidance to those who are new to the sport. So, don't hesitate to reach out, make new friends, and become a part of the rock climbing community in Hvar.


Conclusion: Why Rock Climbing in Hvar is a Must-Try

Rock climbing in Hvar offers an adventure like no other. With its stunning natural beauty, a diverse range of climbing spots, and a warm Mediterranean climate, Hvar is a paradise for climbers of all levels. Whether you're a beginner looking to learn the ropes or an experienced climber seeking a new challenge, Hvar has something to offer. From the limestone cliffs of Sveta Nedilja to the ancient ruins of Dubovica Beach, every climb in Hvar is a unique and unforgettable experience. So, pack your climbing gear, book a guided tour, and embark on a rock climbing adventure in Hvar. Discover the thrill of scaling towering cliffs, take in the breathtaking views, and immerse yourself in the rich history and vibrant rock-climbing community of this Croatian paradise.

  • Sport Climbing: This is the most popular style in Antalya, with numerous bolted routes available. The limestone cliffs offer a variety of grades, accommodating both beginners and advanced climbers.
  • Bouldering: For those who prefer shorter, more intense climbs, bouldering is a fantastic option. Feslekan Yayla, located high in the mountains, is a notable bouldering area that offers stunning views and challenging problems.
  • Multi-Pitch Climbing: For the more adventurous, multi-pitch routes are available in areas like Ala Daglar National Park. These climbs provide a unique challenge and the chance to experience the beauty of the Turkish landscape from different heights.

Safety Considerations

Safety is paramount in any climbing adventure. It’s essential to be aware of the weather conditions and to have the appropriate gear. Always check for route conditions and ensure that your climbing partner is experienced in belaying and safety procedures.

 

Local Climbing Community

One of the highlights of climbing in Antalya is the vibrant local community. Climbers from various backgrounds come together to share their passion for the sport, creating a welcoming environment for newcomers.

Events and Competitions

Throughout the year, Antalya hosts various climbing events, including competitions and festivals. These gatherings are a great way to meet other climbers, learn new skills, and experience the local climbing culture.

Online Platforms and Resources

Several online platforms provide valuable information about climbing in Antalya. Websites and forums dedicated to climbing often feature route descriptions, conditions, and tips from fellow climbers. Engaging with these communities can enhance your experience and help you discover hidden gems.

 

Exploring Beyond Climbing: Other Activities in Antalya

While climbing is undoubtedly a highlight, Antalya has much more to offer.

Hiking and Trekking

The stunning landscapes surrounding Antalya provide excellent opportunities for hiking and trekking. Trails like the Lycian Way offer breathtaking views of the coastline and mountains, making for a perfect rest day between climbing sessions.

Cultural Experiences

Antalya is rich in history and culture. Take some time to explore ancient ruins, such as the Roman theater in Aspendos or the old town of Kaleiçi, where narrow streets are lined with charming cafes and shops.

Beach Relaxation

After a long day of climbing, there’s nothing quite like unwinding on one of Antalya’s beautiful beaches. The warm Mediterranean waters are perfect for a refreshing swim, and the surrounding scenery is simply breathtaking.

 

Preparing for Your Trip: Tips and Tricks

To make the most of your climbing adventure in Antalya, consider these helpful tips.

Packing Essentials

  • Climbing Gear: Ensure you have all your necessary equipment, including shoes, a harness, and a chalk bag. Clothing: The weather can vary, so pack layers to accommodate temperature changes. Lightweight, breathable fabrics are ideal for climbing.
  • Hydration and Nutrition: Stay hydrated and bring snacks to keep your energy levels up while climbing.

Travel Logistics

Getting There: Antalya has an international airport with flights from major cities worldwide. Once you arrive, local transportation options include buses, taxis, and rental cars. Currency and Costs: The local currency is the Turkish Lira. While Antalya is generally affordable, it’s wise to budget for accommodation, food, and climbing fees.

 

Conclusion: Embrace the Climbing Adventure in Antalya


Antalya, with its breathtaking landscapes and diverse climbing opportunities, stands out as a premier destination for rock climbing. The combination of excellent routes, a supportive climbing community, and the chance to explore the rich culture of Turkey makes it an ideal choice for climbers of all levels. Whether you're signing up for a winter sport climbing course with Rockbusters or simply enjoying the stunning views from a cliffside, your adventure in Antalya is sure to be unforgettable.

So pack your gear, gather your friends, and get ready to experience the thrill of climbing in one of the most beautiful locations in the world. Antalya awaits your ascent!
